summary: Rabbi Meir teaches that someone who learns Torah for its own sake earns many good things: he is loved by Hashem and by people, the Torah makes him humble and good, and he becomes like a spring that never stops flowing.

chunks.en: The Sages taught in the language of the Mishnah,
blessed is He Who chose them and their Mishnah.
Rabbi Meir says: Anyone
who learns Torah for its own sake,
earns many things.
And more than that, the whole world
is worth it for him.
chunks.explain: The whole world was worth creating just for him.

chunks.en: He is called a friend,
beloved, he loves Hashem,
he loves people,
he makes Hashem happy,
he makes people happy.
And the Torah dresses him in humility and fear of Hashem,

chunks.he: וּמַכְשַׁרְתּוֹ לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק וְחָסִיד וְיָשָׁר וְנֶאֱמָן,
chunks.en: and makes him fit to be a tzaddik, a chasid, honest and faithful,
and keeps him far from sin,
and brings him close to merit,

chunks.he: וְנֶהֱנִין מִמֶּנּוּ עֵצָה וְתוּשִׁיָּה בִּינָה וּגְבוּרָה,
chunks.en: and people get from him advice and wisdom, understanding and strength,
as it says (Mishlei 8): Mine is advice
and wisdom, I am understanding, mine is strength.

chunks.he: וְנוֹתֶנֶת לוֹ מַלְכוּת וּמֶמְשָׁלָה וְחִקּוּר דִּין,
chunks.en: And it gives him kingship and rule and the power to judge,
and they show him the secrets of the Torah,

chunks.he: וְנַעֲשֶׂה כְמַעְיָן הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר וּכְנָהָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ פוֹסֵק,
chunks.en: and he becomes like a spring that grows stronger and like a river that never stops,
and he is modest and patient,
and he forgives when people insult him,
and it makes him great and lifts him above all creations.

summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi teaches that every day a voice from Har Sinai calls out sadly about people who don't learn Torah. Only someone who learns Torah is truly free, and learning Torah lifts a person up.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Every single day a heavenly voice
goes out from Har Chorev and announces and says:

chunks.he: אוֹי לָהֶם לַבְּרִיּוֹת מֵעֶלְבּוֹנָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה.
chunks.en: Woe to people because of the insult to the Torah.
Because anyone who does not learn
Torah is called rejected by Hashem,
as it says (Mishlei 11): A gold ring in the nose
of a pig, a pretty woman who has no sense.
And it says (Shemos 32): And the Luchos were the work
of Hashem, and the writing was the writing of Hashem,
engraved on the Luchos.
Do not read charus, engraved, but cheirus, freedom,
chunks.explain: The words look the same in Hebrew.

chunks.en: because no one is truly free except
one who is busy learning Torah.
And anyone who is busy learning
Torah, he goes up higher,
as it says (Bamidbar 21): And from Mattanah
to Nachaliel, and from Nachaliel to Bamos.
chunks.explain: From the gift of Torah a person goes up high.

summary: One who learns even a tiny bit of Torah from someone must give him honor. Dovid HaMelech learned only two things from Achitofel and still called him his teacher. And real honor is only Torah.

chunks.he: הַלּוֹמֵד מֵחֲבֵרוֹ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ הֲלָכָה
chunks.en: One who learns from his friend one perek or one

chunks.he: אַחַת אוֹ פָסוּק אֶחָד אוֹ דִבּוּר
chunks.en: halachah or one pasuk or one
saying or even one letter,
must treat him with honor,
because this is what we found with Dovid, king of Yisrael,
who learned from Achitofel nothing but
only two things,
yet he called him his teacher, his guide and his close friend,
as it says (Tehillim 55): But you,
a man like me, my guide and my close friend.
Isn't this a kal vachomer?
chunks.explain: If it is true for the small case, it is surely true for the big one.

chunks.en: If Dovid, king of Yisrael,

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא לָמַד מֵאֲחִיתֹפֶל אֶלָּא שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים
chunks.en: who learned from Achitofel only two things,
still called him his teacher, his guide and his close friend,

chunks.he: הַלּוֹמֵד מֵחֲבֵרוֹ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ הֲלָכָה
chunks.en: one who learns from his friend one perek or one

chunks.he: אַחַת אוֹ פָסוּק אֶחָד אוֹ דִבּוּר
chunks.en: halachah or one pasuk or one
saying or even one letter,
how much more and more so
must he treat him with honor.
And there is no honor but Torah,
as it says (Mishlei 3): The wise will inherit honor,
(Mishlei 28) and the wholehearted will inherit good.
And there is no good but Torah,
as it says (Mishlei 4): For a good teaching
I have given you, do not leave My Torah.

summary: This mishnah teaches that someone who learns Torah may need to live simply, with little food and comfort, and work hard at Torah. If he does, he will be fortunate in this world and in the World to Come.

chunks.en: This is the way of the Torah:
eat bread with salt,
and drink water in small measure,
and sleep on the ground,
and live a hard life,
and work hard in the Torah.
If you do this,
(Tehillim 128) you are fortunate and it is good for you.
You are fortunate in this world, and it is good
for you in the World to Come.

summary: Do not chase after greatness and honor, and do not wish for the tables of kings, because the Torah's table and crown are greater. Hashem will surely pay you for your work.

chunks.en: Do not look for greatness for yourself,
and do not long for honor.
Do more than you learn.
And do not wish for the table of kings,
because your table is greater than their table,
and your crown is greater than their crown,
and your Employer can be trusted
to pay you the reward for your work.

summary: Torah is greater than being a Kohen or a king. It is gained in forty-eight ways, like listening carefully, being humble and happy, asking and answering, and saying something in the name of the person who said it.

chunks.en: Torah is greater than
the Kehunah and the kingship,
because kingship is gained with thirty special qualities,
and the Kehunah with twenty-four,
and the Torah is gained with forty-eight things.
And these are they:
by learning, by listening with the ear,
by saying it clearly with the lips,
by understanding of the heart,
by thinking deeply in the heart,
by awe, by fear,
by humility, by joy,
by purity, by serving the Sages,
by being careful with friends,
chunks.explain: Learning together and checking each other.

chunks.en: and by sharp discussion with students,

words.en: and by the sharp discussion of

chunks.en: by calm thinking, by Chumash,
by Mishnah, by less business,
by less worldly things,
by less pleasure,
by less sleep,
by less chatter,
by less joking,
by being patient,
by a good heart,
by trusting the Sages,
and by accepting suffering,
one who knows his place,
and is happy with his share,

words.en: and the one who is happy

chunks.en: and makes a fence for his words,
and does not take credit for himself,
beloved, loves Hashem,
loves people,
loves tzedakah,
loves fairness,
loves being corrected,
keeps far from honor,
and is not proud of his learning,
and is not happy to give rulings,
helps carry the burden with his friend,
judges him in a good way,
sets him on the truth,
and sets him on peace,
calms his heart in his learning,
asks and answers,
listens and adds,
one who learns in order to teach,
and one who learns in order to do,
one who makes his teacher wiser,
and one who gets exactly right what he heard,

words.en: and the one who makes exact

chunks.en: and one who says a thing in the name of the one who said it.
So you learned that anyone who says a thing
in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world,
as it says (Esther 2): And Esther told
the king in the name of Mordechai.
chunks.explain: That is how Mordechai saved the king, which led to the Purim miracle.

summary: Torah is great, because it gives life to those who keep it in this world and the next. The mishnah brings many pesukim that show how Torah brings life, health, honor and peace.

chunks.en: Torah is great, because it gives life
to those who keep it, in this world and in the World to Come,
as it says (Mishlei 4): For they are life
to those who find them, and healing to all his body.
And it says (there 3): It will be healing
for your body and drink for your bones.
And it says (there 3): A tree of life
is it for those who hold on to it, and those who support it are fortunate.
And it says (there 1): For a wreath
of grace they are for your head, and necklaces for your neck.
And it says (there 4): It will give your head
a wreath of grace, a crown of glory it will give you.
And it says (there 9): For through me your days
will increase, and years of life will be added to you.
And it says (there 3): Long life
is in its right hand, in its left hand riches and honor.
And it says (there): For long life
and years of life and peace they will add to you.
And it says (there): Its ways are ways
of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace.

summary: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai teaches that beauty, strength, wealth, honor, wisdom, old age and children are fitting for tzaddikim. All of these were found in Rebbi and his sons.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehudah in the name of
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
Beauty and strength and wealth and honor
and wisdom and old age and gray hair and children
are fitting for tzaddikim and fitting for the world,
as it says (there 16): A crown of glory
is gray hair, found in the way of tzedakah.
And it says (there 20): The glory of young men
is their strength, and the beauty of old men is gray hair.
And it says (there 14): The crown of the wise is their wealth.
And it says (there 17): The crown of old men
is grandchildren, and the glory of children is their fathers.
And it says (Yeshayah 24): And will be ashamed
the moon, and the sun will be embarrassed,
because Hashem of Hosts will rule on Mount
Tziyon and in Yerushalayim, and before His elders will be honor.
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים לַצַּדִּיקִים,
chunks.en: These seven qualities that the Sages counted for tzaddikim,
all of them came true in Rebbi and his sons.

summary: Rabbi Yosi ben Kisma tells how a man offered him great riches to move to his town, but he said he would live only in a place of Torah, because only Torah and good deeds go with a person after he dies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi ben Kisma said:
Once I was walking on the road,
and a man met me,
and he greeted me with shalom,
and I greeted him back with shalom.
He said to me:
Rabbi, what place are you from?
I said to him:
From a big city of Sages
and of scholars am I.
He said to me:
Rabbi, would you like to live with us in our place?
And I will give you a million
gold coins and precious stones and pearls.
I said to him:

chunks.he: בְּנִי, אִם אַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי כָל כֶּסֶף
chunks.en: My son, even if you give me all the silver
and gold and precious stones and pearls in the world,
I would live only in a place of Torah.
And not only that,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֵין
chunks.en: but when a person leaves this world, nothing

chunks.he: מְלַוִּין לוֹ לָאָדָם לֹא כֶסֶף וְלֹא
chunks.en: goes along with a person, not silver and not
gold and not precious stones and pearls,
but only Torah and good deeds,
as it says (Mishlei 6): When you walk, it will lead you,
when you lie down, it will guard over you,
and when you wake up, it will talk with you.
When you walk, it will lead you,
in this world,
when you lie down, it will guard over you,
in the grave, and when you wake up, it will talk with you,
in the World to Come.

chunks.he: וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים עַל יְדֵי
chunks.en: And so it is written in the book of Tehillim by
Dovid, king of Yisrael (Tehillim 119):
The Torah of Your mouth is better for me
than thousands of gold and silver coins.
And it says (Chaggai 2): Mine is the silver
and Mine is the gold, says Hashem of Hosts.

summary: Hashem made five things especially His own in His world: the Torah, the heavens and earth, Avraham, the Jewish people, and the Beis HaMikdash. The mishnah brings a pasuk for each.

chunks.en: Five special possessions
the Holy One, blessed is He, acquired in His world,
and these are they:
Torah is one possession,
heaven and earth are one possession,
Avraham is one possession,
Yisrael is one possession,
the Beis HaMikdash is one possession.
How do we know Torah?
As it is written (Mishlei 8):
Hashem acquired me as the beginning of His way,
before His works, from long ago.
How do we know heaven and earth are one possession?
As it is written (Yeshayah 66):

chunks.he: כֹּה אָמַר ה' הַשָּׁמַיִם כִּסְאִי וְהָאָרֶץ
chunks.en: So says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth

chunks.he: הֲדֹם רַגְלָי אֵי זֶה בַיִת אֲשֶׁר
chunks.en: is My footstool. Which house

chunks.he: תִּבְנוּ לִי וְאֵי זֶה מָקוֹם מְנוּחָתִי,
chunks.en: can you build for Me, and which place is My resting place?
And it says (Tehillim 104): How many
are Your works, Hashem, You made them all with wisdom,
the earth is full of Your possessions.
How do we know Avraham is one possession?
As it is written (Bereishis 14):
And he blessed him and said: Blessed is Avram to G-d
Most High, Who owns heaven and earth.
How do we know Yisrael is one possession?
As it is written (Shemos 15):
Until Your people cross, Hashem, until
this people that You acquired crosses.
And it says (Tehillim 16): For the holy ones who are in the land,
they and the mighty ones, all My desire is in them.
How do we know the Beis HaMikdash is one possession?
As it is written (Shemos 15):
The place for You to dwell that You made, Hashem,
the Mikdash, Hashem, that Your hands set up.
And it says (Tehillim 78): And He brought them to the border
of His holy place, this mountain that His right hand acquired.

summary: Everything Hashem created, He created for His honor. Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya teaches that Hashem gave Yisrael many mitzvos because He wanted to give them merit.

chunks.en: Everything that the Holy One,
blessed is He, created in His world,
He created only for His honor,
as it says (Yeshayah 43):
Everything that is called by My Name and for My honor,
I created it, I formed it, I also made it.
And it says (Shemos 15):
Hashem will rule forever and ever.
Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya says:
The Holy One, blessed is He, wanted
to give merit to Yisrael,
so He gave them a lot of Torah and mitzvos,
as it says (Yeshayah 42): Hashem wanted,
for the sake of its righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious.
